intro: Flooring removal is priced by the square foot, and anyone who gives you a firm rate before seeing the floor is guessing. What is under the covering is what moves the number — thinset on a clean slab is the straightforward case, and tile over a mortar bed, tile over a second layer of old tile, or glue-down over a wood subfloor are all considerably more work. So rather than publish a rate card we cannot honour on your particular floor, here is exactly what we look at when we price one. Send a photo and the rough square footage and you will get a real number back, free and with no obligation.

cost_table.heading: What Your Quote Depends On
cost_table.lede: Five things move the price on a removal job. If you tell us about them up front, the number you get is the number you pay.
rows: Ceramic and porcelain take more machine time than carpet or floating laminate. Large-format and wood-look plank tile are the most stubborn of all.
Thinset on a bare slab is the easy case. A mortar bed, a second layer of old tile, or a wood subfloor each add labour that cannot be seen from the surface.
Open living areas run faster per foot than a house full of small rooms, closets and tight thresholds where the machine cannot reach.
How much prep the slab needs
Leftover adhesive, mastic and high spots have to be ground off before anything new goes down. Some slabs need very little; some need a full pass.

Ground-floor with a driveway is straightforward. Third-floor condo with elevator-only access, association hours and shared corridors is not — and neither is a house or office you are still living and working in.
cost_table.footnote: Removal, adhesive grinding, debris haul-off and disposal are quoted as one price. There is no separate charge for the dust containment — it is how we work, not an upgrade.

notes: Quotes are free and carry no obligation. Prep-only jobs are welcome if another company already pulled your floor and left you with a slab your installer will not work over.
